Rule: A.1 item 34 'Computer's coded character set (for literals, correspondence between compile-time and runtime character sets, when conversion takes place). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon there being a difference between the compile-time and runtime computer's coded character sets. This item, if provided ... shall be documented'. §8.1.2: 'The implementor shall define the correspondence of each character of the compile-time coded character set with an associated character in the runtime coded character set' (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 3)). Code: the compile-time computer's coded character set (the set 'used in the memory of the computer during compilation', §8.1.2 first sentence) is the .NET UTF-16 string the source is decoded into by CompilationInputs.ReadAllText; literals are emitted as C# string literals and the runtime alphanumeric/national sets are the same UTF-16 code units, so NO compile-time->runtime conversion exists (probe cs1.cob: VALUE '€é' -> ORD 8365 at run time, i.e. the compile-time character unchanged). The condition the item is conditioned on (a difference between the sets) does not arise; the facility is absent. CONFORMANCE.md states neither the identity nor the absence (no DOC-A.1-34 row), and PB690 (open) already names 'DOC-A.1-31/-34 rows' as owed - though PB690's file-encoding question is really item 31's, not item 34's (item 34 is literals only). Recorded NOT-IMPLEMENTED (facility absent) pending an owner-level posture for conditional items whose condition is unmet (finding conditional-facility-absent-posture). Owning note: PB690 (open).

Rule: A.1 item 36 'Computer's coded character set (when composite alphanumeric and national, mapping of characters to each). This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support for a composite alphanumeric and national computer character set. This item, if provided ... shall be documented'. §8.1.2 'When these are implemented as one character set, the implementor shall specify the characters that map into the computer's alphanumeric coded character set and the characters that map into the computer's national coded character set' (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 3)). Owning note: none names item 36 (grep 'DOC-A.1-36\|item 36' hits only Annex E.3.3 item 36 notes PB434/PB438/PB441/PB595); PB690 (open, blocked on owner) owns the file-encoding half and names rows 31/34. Rule: A.1 item 39 'CONTINUE statement (precision and maximum size of the arithmetic expression specifying the number of seconds to pause execution) This item is required. This item shall be documented'. §14.9.9.4 GR1: 'The implementor shall specify the value of m, which may be zero, and the value of n, which shall be greater than zero' (cite.py --check 14.9.9.4 -> OK §14.9.9.4 1)); 'The implementor shall specify the maximum meaningful value of arithmetic-expression-1' -> OK §14.9.9.4 1); 'If the value arithmetic-expression-1 is greater than this maximum meaningful value, the maximum meaningful value is placed into the temporary data item' -> OK §14.9.9.4 1). CONFORMANCE.md: NO '| DOC-A.1-39 |' row. Only m is stated, in §2 A.3 row 8 ('Implementor m = 0 (integer seconds)'); n is stated nowhere and the maximum (CobolTiming.MaxSeconds = 86_400) lives only in a code comment. TWO defects: (1) documentation - missing row (harm silent), owned by PB160 (open: 'CONTINUE item 39 (precision + 86,400 max live only in a code comment)'), referenced not re-reported. (2) NEW, wrong-answer: the maximum-meaningful-value clamp is applied AFTER an unchecked narrowing to long, so an interval beyond 2^63 wraps. StatementEmitter emits '(long)(x.Expr)' (Scale-0 lane) / '(long)(...).ToUnscaled(0, Truncation)' (Dec lane) and SleepTruncated does Math.Min(secs, MaxSeconds) on the already-wrapped value. Probe /tmp/adj/probe/ca2.cob (--std default 2023): 'CONTINUE AFTER 18446744073709551619 SECONDS' suspends ~3 s (wall 5.4 s vs 2.4 s baseline) and 'CONTINUE AFTER 18446744073709551616 SECONDS' suspends 0 s; probe ca.cob with 01 BIG PIC 9(20) VALUE 2^64 likewise returns at once. GR1 requires the maximum meaningful value (86,400 s) to be placed in the temporary for any value above it. The Real (float) lane is safe ((long)double saturates, then Min). No kb/Work note owns the wrap (grep of CONTINUE AFTER notes for wrap/overflow: PB241/PB138/PB463 do not cover it; PB463 is the sibling pattern for SET SIZE OF). Finding: continue-after-interval-wraps-before-clamp.

Rule: A.1 item 49 'DEFINE directive (mechanism for providing value of a compilation-variable-name from the operating environment). This item is required. This item shall be documented ... (7.3.11, DEFINE directive, General rule 4)'. §7.3.11.4 GR4 'If the PARAMETER phrase is specified, the value referenced by compilation-variable-name-1 is obtained from the operating environment by an implementor-defined method when the DEFINE directive is processed. If no value is made available from the operating environment, compilation-variable-name-1 is not defined' (cite.py --check 7.3.11.4 -> OK §7.3.11.4 4)). CONFORMANCE.md: no '| DOC-A.1-49 |' row and no mention of the PARAMETER mechanism anywhere (grep 'PARAMETER phrase', '7.3.11'). Code fixes the mechanism: the process environment variable whose name is the compilation-variable-name AS SPELLED in the directive (Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(name), no case folding); unset -> the name is removed (GR4's 'not defined', met); a value that parses as an invariant-culture decimal is numeric, otherwise alphanumeric. Probe /tmp/adj/probe/def.cob ('>>DEFINE MyVar AS PARAMETER' / '>>IF MyVar IS DEFINED'): no env -> NOT-DEFINED; MYVAR=x -> NOT-DEFINED; MyVar=x -> DEFINED; NUMV=7 -> numeric, '>>IF NUMV > 5' true. So the value source depends on the SPELLING of a case-insensitive COBOL word (MyVar and MYVAR name the same compilation variable but read different environment variables on a case-sensitive host) - a legitimate implementor choice only if documented, and it is not. Harm: silent. Owning notes: none names A.1 item 49 (PB1369 covers items 23/40/53/54 of §7; PB1367 (open) owns the DEFINE general-format / SR2 bypass on the PARAMETER arm, a different defect). New finding: define-parameter-mechanism-undocumented-and-spelling-sensitive.

editions: 2023 (DELETE FILE is format 2 of §14.9.10, a 2023 addition per CONFORMANCE §2 row 31)
notes: Rule: A.1 item 51 'DELETE FILE statement (effects of the DELETE file statement). This item is required. This item shall be documented ... (14.9.10, DELETE statement, General rule 20)'. §14.9.10.4 GR20 'If the execution of the DELETE FILE statement is successful, the file is deleted if it exists or no action takes place if the mass storage file does not exist' (cite.py --check 14.9.10.4 -> OK §14.9.10.4 20)). The implementor-defined content is what 'the file is deleted' DOES on this platform. CONFORMANCE.md: no '| DOC-A.1-51 |' row. Adjacent determinations exist but answer other questions: DOC-A.1-50 (GR19, validated attribute set EMPTY), §3 '⚖ DETERMINATION — the DELETE FILE statement's GR20/GR21 are internally contradictory' (control-flow reading, PB141), §2 row 31 (Claimed). Code fixes the effect (FileRegistry.DeleteFile): a single host File.Delete of the connector's resolved HostPath - no sidecar/index/lock artifact is removed ('NOTHING ELSE IS DELETED, and the absence is the design (kb/Work PB802)'); a bare ASSIGN USING connector with no association yet is '05' without touching any file; presence probed through HostFile.Probe ('05' absent / '37' unauthorized); a file held by another connector or run unit is '62' and not deleted; IOException maps to '37'/'30' (ForDeleteFileFailure). None of that - in particular that deletion is an OS unlink of exactly one path and what happens on a POSIX host to a file another process holds - is stated in the user documentation. Undocumented determination => DIVERGES, harm silent. Owning note: none names A.1 item 51 (grep empty); register umbrella PB160/A11. Clustered into finding a1-register-rows-missing.

Rule: A.1 item 52 'Devices that allow concurrent access. This item is required. This item shall be documented ... (9.1.15, Sharing mode)'. §9.1.15 'A shared physical file shall reside on a device that allows concurrent access to the file. The implementor shall specify which devices allow concurrent access to a physical file' (cite.py --check 9.1.15 -> OK §9.1.15). A.4.7 File sharing and record locking is Claimed (CONFORMANCE §5), so the item is live. CONFORMANCE.md: no '| DOC-A.1-52 |' row and no statement naming the devices (grep 'concurrent' / 'device' in the sharing context: nothing). Code fixes an implicit answer: every host path a file connector resolves to is treated as concurrently accessible - the Table-19 arbiter admits sibling connectors of this run unit and FileLockPosture maps the sharing mode onto a .NET FileShare for other run units, with no device classification at all (a character device, pipe or /dev/stdout assign target is handled like a mass-storage file); on Linux/macOS .NET's FileShare is one advisory flock, so §9.1.15 2)'s file lock has no expression there (PB833, open). The determination is unmade and undocumented => DIVERGES, harm silent. Owning note: PB322 (open) - 'B. Which devices allow concurrent access — A.1 items 52 and 76'. Referenced, not re-reported.
